title: The Value Added Tax (Distance Selling) (Amendments) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend Schedules 9ZD, 9ZE and Part 3 of Schedule 9ZF to the Value Added Tax Act 1994 and come into force on 1st January 2027. They implement certain amendments made by Council Directive (EU) 2025/516 to Council Directive 2006/112/EC (“the VAT Directive”), pursuant to the United Kingdom’s obligations under the Windsor Framework.

The Government Resources and Accounts (Northern Ireland) Act 2001 (Estimates and Accounts) (Designation of Bodies) (Amendment) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Government Resources and Accounts (Northern Ireland) Act 2001 (Estimates and Accounts) (Designation of Bodies) Order 2026 (S.I. 2026 No. 49) (“the principal Order”), which designates specified central government bodies in relation to named government departments for the purpose of those departments’ supply estimates and resource accounts.

title: The Online Safety Act 2023 (Commencement No. 8) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations are the eighth commencement regulations made under the Online Safety Act 2023 (c. 50) (“the Act”). They bring into force section 75 of the Act which places duties on providers of Category 1, 2A and 2B services to set out their policies on disclosing information to the parents of deceased child users, have a dedicated helpline or section of the service (or similar means) for such parents, provide details about the relevant policies and procedures in their terms of service or a publicly available statement, and respond in a timely manner to requests for information. Section 75 also requires the providers to operate a complaints procedure in relation to these duties.

title: The Rehabilitation of Offenders (Exceptions) (Amendment No. 2) Order (Northern Ireland) 2026
summary: This Order amends the Rehabilitation of Offenders (Exceptions) Order (Northern Ireland) 1979 (“the 1979 Order”) to bring individuals who are seeking to assess children and vulnerable adults as registered health care professionals employed or engaged by the Department for Communities, or by its contractors or sub-contractors, who are carrying out activities for the Department for Communities, within the excluded circumstances set out in Article 2 of the 1979 Order.

title: The Police Act 1997 (Criminal Records) (Amendment No. 2) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Police Act 1997 (Criminal Records) (Disclosure) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2008 (“the 2008 Regulations”) to make provision for enhanced criminal record checks with suitability information in relation to individuals who are seeking to assess children and vulnerable adults as registered Health Care Professionals employed or engaged by the Department for Communities, or by its contractors or sub-contractors, who are carrying out activities for the Department for Communities.

title: The Railways (Interoperability in Northern Ireland) (Convention on International Carriage by Rail) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations implement Directive (EU) 2016/797 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2016 on the interoperability of the rail system within the European Union (O.J. No. L 138, 26.5.2016, p. 44) (the “2016 Directive”) for Northern Ireland, making technical provision for the placing on the market, putting into service and free movement of railway products. The 2016 Directive is a recast of Directive 2008/57/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 17 June 2008 (O.J. No. L 191, 18.7.2008, p. 1), which was transposed for Great Britain and Northern Ireland by way of the Railways (Interoperability) Regulations 2011 (S.I. 2011/3066). These Regulations replace that regime for Northern Ireland in line with the UK’s obligations pursuant to Article 5(4) and Annex II of the Windsor Framework.

title: The Critical Third Parties (Designation) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations designate BlackRock Financial Management, Inc., Bloomberg L.P., Bottomline Technologies Limited, Broadridge Financial Solutions Limited and Form3 UK Limited as critical third parties. The Regulations amend the Critical Third Parties (Designation) Regulations 2026 (S.I. 2026/777) to add the entities to the list of designated critical third parties.

title: The Human Rights Act 1998 (Remedial) Order 2026
summary: This Order amends the Human Rights Act 1998 (“the HRA”) to address a finding of the European Court of Human Rights of a breach of Article 13 of the European Convention on Human Rights (“the Convention”) in the case of S.W. v United Kingdom (Application no. 87/18).

title: The Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector and Social Rented Sector (England) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector and Social Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 (S.I. 2020/312) (“the Principal Regulations”).

title: The Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) (Amendment) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations amend the Hazards in Social Housing (Prescribed Requirements) (England) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/1042) (“the 2025 Regulations”), also known as “Awaab’s Law”, which prescribe requirements with which a landlord of social housing is required to comply by virtue of the covenant implied by section 10A(2) of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 (c. 70).

title: The Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act 2025 (Specified Purposes Related to Policing) Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations specify purposes related to policing for the purposes of sections 30 to 34 of the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act 2025 (c. 31) (“the 2025 Act”).

title: The Statement of Trade Union Rights Regulations 2026
summary: These Regulations make provision about the written statement which an employer is required to give to a worker under section 136A of the Trade Union and Labour Relations (Consolidation) Act 1992 (“the 1992 Act”). Section 136A was inserted into the 1992 Act by section 58 of the Employment Rights Act 2025 (“the 2025 Act”).
